vocabulary.meaning_en: an official card that says you can drive a car
vocabulary.example: You need a driver's license to drive a car.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to succeed in a test or exam
vocabulary.example: She passed her English exam.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a test to see if you can drive safely
vocabulary.example: I have my driving test tomorrow.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to pay money to use something for a time
vocabulary.example: We rented a car for the weekend.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to control a car and make it move
vocabulary.example: My father drives to work every day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: machines used on a farm, like tractors
vocabulary.note_ar: equipment اسم غير معدود: لا نقول equipments.
vocabulary.example: Anna can drive farm equipment very well.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a little afraid or worried
vocabulary.example: I'm always nervous before a test.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the cars and buses on a road
vocabulary.example: There is a lot of traffic in the city in the morning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take place
vocabulary.example: What happened at school today?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a belt in a car that keeps you safe in your seat
vocabulary.example: Always wear your seatbelt.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to close a belt
vocabulary.example: Is your seatbelt buckled?

vocabulary.meaning_en: the machine that makes a car move
vocabulary.example: The car's engine is very loud.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the part you push with your foot to make a car go faster
vocabulary.example: Don't push the gas pedal too hard.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to change direction
vocabulary.example: Turn left at the bank.

vocabulary.meaning_en: nearly; but not completely
vocabulary.example: I almost missed the bus.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to touch something hard and fast
vocabulary.example: The ball hit the window.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to shout loudly
vocabulary.note_ar: yell at someone = يصرخ في وجه أحد.
vocabulary.note_en: yell at someone = shout angrily at someone.
vocabulary.example: Please don't yell at me.

vocabulary.meaning_en: feeling fear
vocabulary.example: I was afraid of the big dog.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make a car slow down or stop; the part that does this
vocabulary.note_ar: تُنطق مثل break (يكسر) لكن المعنى مختلف.
vocabulary.note_en: Sounds like "break" but the meaning is different.
vocabulary.example: Brake! There is a car in front of us!

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make a loud sound with a car horn
vocabulary.example: Why is that driver honking?

vocabulary.meaning_en: not fast
vocabulary.note_ar: في الكلام اليومي يقولون drive slow، والأصح نحوياً drive slowly.
vocabulary.note_en: In everyday speech people say "drive slow"; "slowly" is the standard adverb.
vocabulary.example: You were driving too slow.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the round part you hold to drive a car (steering wheel)
vocabulary.example: Keep both hands on the wheel.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the people whose job is to keep order and stop crime
vocabulary.note_ar: police اسم جمع: The police are here.
vocabulary.note_en: "Police" takes a plural verb: The police are here.
vocabulary.example: The police stopped the car.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very bad
vocabulary.example: The weather was awful yesterday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to do something many times to get better
vocabulary.note_ar: في بريطانيا الفعل practise والاسم practice.
vocabulary.note_en: UK: the verb is "practise", the noun is "practice".
vocabulary.example: I practiced every day and passed the test.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give an answer when you are not sure
vocabulary.example: Guess what? I got the job!

fine_lines.title: brake vs break
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الكلمتان تُنطقان بنفس الطريقة. brake = يفرمل / الفرامل في السيارة. break = يكسر، أو استراحة قصيرة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: The two words sound the same. Brake = stop or slow a car (or the part that does it). Break = make something go into pieces, or a short rest.

fine_lines.title: almost vs most
fine_lines.explanation_ar: almost = تقريباً / كاد (الشيء لم يحدث تماماً). most = معظم / أغلب. You almost hit that car = كدتِ تصطدمين بتلك السيارة (لكنك لم تصطدمي).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Almost = nearly, but not really. Most = the biggest part of something. "You almost hit that car" means you nearly hit it but did not.

fine_lines.title: yell vs yell at
fine_lines.explanation_ar: yell = يصرخ بصوت عالٍ (مثلاً لينادي أحداً بعيداً). yell at someone = يصرخ في وجه شخص، غالباً بغضب.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Yell = shout loudly (for example, to call someone far away). Yell at someone = shout at a person, usually in anger.

expressions.meaning_en: Said before you tell someone surprising news.
expressions.example: Guess what? I passed my test!

expressions.meaning_en: I succeeded in the driving test.
expressions.example: My brother passed his driving test on the first try.

expressions.phrase: Did you pass the test the first time?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل نجحت في الاختبار من أول مرة؟
expressions.meaning_en: Asking if someone succeeded on their first try.
expressions.example: "Did you pass the test the first time?" "No, the second time."
You finished your homework. Good job!

expressions.phrase: You don't need to be nervous.
expressions.meaning_en: There is no reason to worry.
expressions.example: It's an easy test. You don't need to be nervous.

expressions.meaning_ar: من فضلك لا تصرخ في وجهي.
expressions.example: I'm trying my best. Please don't yell at me.
"I lost my bag on the bus." "That sounds awful."

expressions.meaning_ar: لم تسر الأمور على ما يرام.
expressions.example: My first interview did not go well.

expressions.phrase: I guess we walk from here!
expressions.meaning_en: I think we must walk now.
expressions.example: The road is closed. I guess we walk from here!

grammar.title: Simple past questions with did
grammar.explanation_ar: لسؤال في الماضي البسيط نستخدم: Did + الفاعل + الفعل الأساسي؟ لا نضع الفعل في الماضي بعد did، لأن did تحمل معنى الماضي. Did you pass? (وليس Did you passed?). والإجابة القصيرة: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. ومع أدوات الاستفهام: What happened? / Where did you go?
grammar.explanation_en: To ask a question in the simple past use: Did + subject + base verb? Do not put the main verb in the past after did, because did already shows the past: Did you pass? (not Did you passed?). Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. With question words: Where did you go? (But with "What happened?" what is the subject, so there is no did.)
examples: Did you get your driver's license? - I did!
Did you pass the test the first time? - No.
What happened during the first test?

grammar.title: Negative simple past: didn't + base verb
grammar.explanation_ar: النفي في الماضي: didn't (did not) + الفعل الأساسي. I didn't know (وليس I didn't knew).
grammar.explanation_en: For the negative, use didn't (did not) + base verb: I didn't know (not I didn't knew).
examples: She didn't pass the first time.

grammar.title: did for emphasis
grammar.explanation_ar: في الجملة المثبتة يمكن أن نضع did قبل الفعل الأساسي للتأكيد، خاصة عندما نصحّح فكرة سابقة: But I did pass the second time = لكني فعلاً نجحت في المرة الثانية. ننطق did بقوة.
grammar.explanation_en: In a positive sentence we can put did before the base verb to make it stronger, often to correct an idea: "But I did pass the second time." We say "did" strongly.
examples: I didn't pass the first time, but I did pass the second time.
I did call you! Check your phone.

grammar.title: Past continuous: was/were + -ing
grammar.explanation_ar: لوصف حدث كان مستمراً في لحظة في الماضي: was/were + فعل ينتهي بـ ing. You were yelling = كنتَ تصرخ. You were driving too slow = كنتِ تقودين ببطء شديد.
grammar.explanation_en: To talk about an action in progress at a time in the past: was/were + verb-ing.
examples: I was driving in heavy traffic.

questions.question: ___ you pass the test the first time?
questions.explanation_ar: سؤال في الماضي يبدأ بـ Did.
questions.explanation_en: A simple past question starts with "Did".

questions.question: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد did نستخدم الفعل الأساسي get.
questions.explanation_en: After "did" we use the base verb "get".

questions.question: "Did you pass?" "Yes, I ___."
questions.explanation_en: The short answer is "Yes, I did."

questions.question: Choose the correct negative.
questions.explanation_ar: النفي في الماضي: didn't + الفعل الأساسي.

questions.question: "I didn't pass the first time, but I ___ pass the second time." (emphasis)
questions.explanation_en: "Did" before the base verb adds emphasis.

questions.question: What do you wear in a car to stay safe?
questions.explanation_en: A seatbelt keeps you safe in your seat.

questions.question: "Brake!" means:
choices: Stop or slow down the car!
questions.explanation_ar: brake = يفرمل ليوقف السيارة أو يبطئها.
questions.explanation_en: Brake means slow down or stop the car.

questions.question: "You almost hit that car." Did Anna hit the car?
choices: No, but she came very close.
questions.explanation_ar: almost = كادت، أي لم يحدث فعلاً.
questions.explanation_en: "Almost" means it nearly happened, but it did not.

questions.question: "I'm worried about my driving test. I'm very ___."
questions.explanation_ar: nervous = متوتر وقلق، وهي تناسب القلق من الاختبار.
questions.explanation_en: "Nervous" means a little afraid or worried, like before a test.
